Despite all the media hype, I don't believe Greeks are buying bitcoins at all, at least not enough to make a significant difference. I think the media lately has been really overblowing the reports that "Greeks may be rushing into Bitcoin".

Yes, Google searches for “Bitcoin” are increasing in Greece. Yes, there are increased Coinbase and other exchange sign-ups in Greece.

But how could Greeks possibly buy bitcoins in the current conditions?

I'm not aware of all the facts, but I’ve done quite a bit of research on this and I have a background in policy and economics. Here's what I think is happening (I also have a solution).

Recap: why Greeks need Bitcoin

The Greek people need Bitcoin protect themselves from horrible fate that it seems has already / will a near future fall upon them: capital controls, retroactive taxation of bank deposits, banning of online payment methods and most scary of all - banks being forced by, and colluding with, the socialist government leaving the Eurozone and forcibly changing the currency of everyone's bank deposits from Euros to Drachmas.

For obvious reasons, Bitcoin offers a solution to this problem. When discussing with the media (recently: the Senate of Canada report), I often referred to Greece and used the analogy of a Bitcoin as a"lifeboat".

I don't think Bitcoin's usecase is to buy coffee without handling cash or credit cards. THIS is what Bitcoin was made for. It is important to exploit this use-case and demonstrate Bitcoin's potential. In addition, I sincerely believe that getting bitcoins in the hands of Greeks is the most efficient way to help this country. Becoming a Bitcoin broker in Greece, in my opinion, is a humanitarian activity that can also be profitable.

Why Greeks can't buy bitcoins, or why there is no supply

  • Professional OTC sellers and ATM operators, localbitcoin traders and Mycelium traders would be crazy to sell their bitcoins without a way of quickly being able to buy back bitcoins at a fast turnaround rate. The LAST thing that a professional Bitcoiner wants is to be stuck with euros or drachmas when shit hits the fan and the price of Bitcoin goes up.

  • Getting a supply of bitcoins with cash: buying bitcoins off-exchange for cash with the intention of re-selling them (what Bitcoin brokers normally do) is near impossible. Unless there are large scale mining operators, it is hard to imagine how they could secure a consistent supply of bitcoins off market for cash, at least in a way that does not involve money laundering. Who would sell large amounts of bitcoins for cash or bank transfers? Even if Greeks accept Bitcoin payments, how are the clients acquiring bitcoins?

  • Potential Bitcoin brokers / traders / buyers probably can't deposit cash directly on exchanges. I am now aware of available direct deposits with cash that has already been shut down (or could and will soon). In other countries, there are methods of depositing cash indirectly on exchanges without a bank account (e.g. in-person bill payment) but I don’t think (or know) that this exists in Greece.

  • They probably have a lot of difficulty to deposit on exchanges from their banks. Without being 100% aware of the situation, I’d wager this option is now impossible. If there is one thing that banks and government don't like: wires and transfers out of the country. ESPECIALLY for the acquisition of liquid financial stores of value like Bitcoin.

  • Even if they can use bank accounts to buy bitcoins on exchanges, who would be crazy enough to deposit cash into Greek banks right now?

There are many other problems caused by capital controls, bank censorship and so called "anti-money laundering regulations and policies".

Conclusion: Bitcoin sellers need a way of quickly transforming the euros/drachmas they get from selling bitcoins back into bitcoins quickly and without taking a massive hit which would affect their profitability and dis-incentive them from selling bitcoins.

So how can we get bitcoins in the hands of greeks?

The following takes into account the assumption that although Greeks can't withdraw cash anymore, many have been "keeping cash under the mattress" for a while and thus CAN purchase bitcoins with cash if they want to and if there is supply. I've been told this is the case by MSB operators there.

  • Step 1: identify a safe and easily imported / distributed Greek export like olive oil, wine, etc.
  • Step 2: identify a large importer in a country where bitcoins can be easily bought (e.g. Canada)
  • Step 3: find a way for the settlement of the payment from the importer and exporter to be concluded in bitcoins to ensure that bitcoins can make their way to Greece This can be done in two ways.
  • Step 4a: the importer purchase bitcoins from a local broker in the importing country. The importer than pays the exporter in bitcoins. The exporter “cashes-out” those bitcoins with large-scale Bitcoin sellers in Greece. Broker in Greece now has steady supply of bitcoins for cash.
  • Step 4b: Bitcoin brokers in Greece find a way of themselves purchasing exports / entering in export contracts. They pay for these exports in the cash they receive from selling bitcoins. When cargo arrives at destination, partner in the importing country sells the export to a distributor and uses the money to buy bitcoins on an exchange or off-exchange. Bitcoins are then sent back to Greece. Preferably, the bitcoins are sent as soon as possible, ideally only few days after the exports are paid for in Greece.

Of all the ways of getting bitcoins to Greece, this is the only one I’ve thought of that could be legal and convenient. Yes, there is massive overhead which means that the Greek Bitcoin broker’s profitability can be difficult to achieve. But there is two ways this can be mitigated:

  • The person selling bitcoins to the importer is part of the same operation as the person buying bitcoins in Greece for resale. This means they can lower the premium on both ends.
  • High premium: I think a premium of 10-15% is likely. Bitcoin seller could go to 30% premium and still get customers. This is not ideal, but 70% of something is better than 100% of nothing.
  • Exporters and importers would probably prefer that the whole fiat settlement remain in cash. They are less exposed to the risk of bank bail-ins and capital controls. If they can store large amounts of cash, they are probably willing to themselves take a hit and pay a high fee for the settlement to occur in Bitcoin (with guarantee of getting cash in Greece afterwards). This can offset the cost passed down to consumers.

Thoughts?

For reference: I am Francis Pouliot and I run Satoshi Counter, a large-scale physical Bitcoin exchange/OTC trading desk (based out of the Bitcoin Embassy building) in Montreal.

Reddit has a lot of "meta" subs, and it also has a lot of diverse viewpoints come up frequently in its default subs, simply due to the broad and varied demographics visiting those subs. Because of this, a Reddit user is able to approximate what the Reddit community is up to as a whole by evaluating how various topics are introduced and received within those subs. It's a useful functionality. Where should a Voat user go to find similar samples of its general userbase? Where is the "voice" of the Voat community best represented?
What are some good subverse subscriptions that will help the Voat user gain a "big picture" understanding of the Voat community and its collective mind?

I don't want a collective mind here. I want users to have their own thoughts and bring those into well put together discussions.

My advice to users is this: contribute. By contributing, you make your voice heard, are able to start and engage in discussion and the creation of content. This ultimately helps voat to grow and foster the ideals of free speech. By not contributing, a hive mind is more likely and easier to develop. The rest of this post is what I think I'd helpful in "contributing".

If you have trouble finding threads to contribute to (eg the interesting front page posts already have says everything there is to say) start looking at the New or Incoming or Hot tabs, rather than Top. Start your own threads. Head over to /v/chatbox and see what people are interested in (though as a "hall of fame" member over there, I admit it can be a very silly place).

Whatever interests you have, or beliefs you hold, subscribe to verses about those things and to verses that challenge them. This prevents you from being in an echo chamber, circle jerking yourself.

To add: the repeated [inside] jokes, novelty accounts, as so forth- that have been over used for upvotes/ (upvoats?) are part of what led to the cheapening of reddit to begin with, but it seems to be jumping to voat almost instantly... look at how many "PM_ME_YOUR_..." accounts there are now (in the last couple of months).

Be original, take the time to think things through, instead of constantly playing to the crowd.

Perhaps i'm getting old, but the value of the internet, and internet based communities should be to educate yourself and expand your world view, not assimilate with some hive-mind.
